Review scope

Draft for owner review. Structure matters; style is provisional. This is the first Stitch-based trial of the UI documentation process, not an approved final interface or a working Android app. “Async Table” is a working mockup title only.

Review editions: PDF download · Markdown source.

Both portrait and landscape are required (D-290). Each screen below has a 412 × 892 portrait capture and an 892 × 412 landscape capture. These are logical pixel/dp-like design viewports, not physical screen pixels or a promise about every Android device. The landscape image is a real rendering of the responsive design at the short, wide viewport—not a rotated or stretched portrait image.

The pilot covers account entry, navigation, games/invitations, contacts, saved decks, import and lobby preparation. Gameplay, history, combat, reveal, card menus, communication and end-of-play overlays are not designed here. G00 and U01 contain deliberately empty gameplay areas; their rectangles do not settle the eventual board layout.

Reading the mockups

  • Text button: a labeled action such as “Ready” or “Accept.” A leading icon does not turn it into an unlabeled icon button.
  • Icon button: Back arrow or password-visibility eye. The proposed normal target is at least 48 × 48 logical pixels, with an accessible name.
  • Label/status: descriptive text such as “Ready,” “Invitation pending,” or a card count. A checkmark complements text rather than replacing it with color.
  • Field: an explicitly labeled text input, search input or multiline pasted list. Password contents are not silently trimmed or normalized.
  • Thumbnail: an abstract placeholder with a card-name fallback. No production card artwork was requested for this pilot.
  • Muted action: unavailable, with a visible reason. It is not a future feature hidden behind a paywall or an instruction to bypass a failed requirement.
  • Scroll: long lists and forms scroll within their content panel. Main actions must remain reachable in both orientations; an initial viewport is not the entire possible list. On-screen keyboard, large-text and split-screen variants still need their own later visual checks.

Typical draft dimensions: 24 px system-status allowance, 56 px app bar, 16 px outer margins, 12 px gaps, 48 px controls and a 16 px bottom safe-area allowance. These are review targets, not measured native Android implementation claims. Different operating-system insets will change the usable area.

Important: these are static mockups. Their behavior is specified in the notes, not demonstrated by functioning buttons. An incidental label/decoration in a generated image does not authorize a feature that contradicts those notes.

Navigation overview

Sign in ↔ Create account
   └─ Forgot password → email link → New password → Sign in
Main menu
   ├─ Play → Accept invitation → same lobby
   │       ├─ New game → Contacts → Invite → waiting lobby
   │       ├─ Open lobby → choose/prepare deck → Ready
   │       └─ Open active game → gameplay placeholder
   ├─ Manage decks → deck details → rename / cover / re-import / delete
   │              └─ Import → resolve all entries → save new or replace
   ├─ Contacts → username search → Add contact → Invite
   ├─ Android notification settings → operating-system settings
   └─ Logout → signed-out entry
Lobby → both Ready → gameplay placeholder

Back leaves a screen; it is not a game cancellation, Ready withdrawal, gameplay Undo or publication step. Rotation preserves the current screen and surviving in-process input/selection; it does not repeat a request or submit an unfinished form. Saved decks, contacts and games synchronize across devices, but unfinished forms and personal navigation are not automatically cross-device shared state.

Layout choices being proposed

The following are UI proposals, not new behavior approvals: a distinct Contacts destination, its “Invite” placement, list/grid arrangements, bounded authentication forms, two-column landscape panels, import review/save routing, cover-selection confirmation, destructive-action dialogs and the read-only reconnect escape. “Random” is selected in the example lobby state; these images do not choose a universal initial starter default or retention policy.

Existing rules are applied without asking for approval again: no guest/social login, contact approval, full saved-deck builder, score archive, host Start, extra Send, online-presence requirement, automatic opening draw, in-game Sideboard or in-app notification mute controls.

Source of behavior

The primary repository source is docs/design/03-contracts/accounts-decks-and-lobby.md. The Android experience contract and technical notification profile add platform/recovery constraints. These source references are repository documents, not extra pages required to read the hosted packet. Decision references below identify already agreed behavior; the particular control geometry remains proposed.

Suggested review

Refer to a screen ID and orientation, for example “L04 landscape: make the sideboard narrower.” Review the hierarchy, approximate space allocation, icon-versus-text choices, visibility of actions and the state transitions. Colors, fonts, borders and the working name can be ignored for this pilot.

A01 — Sign in

Layout: portrait gives the form a bounded central column; landscape moves the modest app intro beside the form instead of enlarging the fields. Email and Password are text fields; the eye is an icon button. Sign in, Create account and Forgot password are labeled actions. The image deliberately includes an example credential error; a clean initial form omits that message.

Interaction: Sign in submits credentials. Failure keeps inputs available for correction; success opens the main menu or resumes the same-account return context. A valid existing login skips this screen across ordinary restarts and inactivity. No guest entry, alternate social provider or routine session expiry. Password visibility is personal UI only. Back does not sign another device out.

Basis: D-188, D-197, D-217, D-249, D-268, D-289.

A02 — Create account

Layout: Username, Email and Password are fields. The password eye is an icon; Create account and Sign in are text actions. Landscape uses the width for an intro/form split and allows the form panel to scroll, not smaller touch targets.

Interaction: registration uses these three credentials; username is public player identity while email is private. Invalid input/network failure stays on this form with a specific inline explanation and preserved editable input. The proposed successful route returns to A01 with a success notice and known email populated; it does not invent an email-verification gate. No confirmation password, social login or profile editor is required by this draft. Password whitespace/Unicode handling stays consistent with sign-in and reset.

Basis: D-197, D-249; success navigation and exact feedback are UI proposals.

A02b — Registration: lower form

Same screen, different scroll position: the short landscape form panel is scrolled to its bottom to expose Create account and the Sign in link at full touch size. The portrait form fits already, so that capture is unchanged. This is not a separate registration step, new server state or submission. It makes the landscape scrolling cost visible rather than hiding it in the tap budget.

A03 — Password reset email

Layout: one Email field, Send reset link text button, neutral submitted-state notice and Back to sign in. The initial state uses the same structure without the submitted notice. The sample email is synthetic, not account data.

Interaction: request an email reset link without revealing whether that address is registered. A delivery/request failure keeps the address editable and shows a retryable inline error; it does not claim the password changed. Merely requesting or opening a reset link does not revoke sessions. The successful email-link flow continues at A04, not an invented six-digit-code screen.

Basis: D-197, D-279; neutral response follows the authentication profile.

A04 — Set a new password

Layout: New password is a field; its eye is an icon button. Change password is a text button. The valid reset-link state is shown. Email and username are not additional editable account settings here.

Interaction: successful reset changes the password and revokes existing sessions for new requests, then returns to Sign in with a success notice. An expired/invalid/already-used link instead shows a non-actionable error and a Request another link route to A03; it does not submit a reset or revoke sessions. Do not silently trim password contents. Already-authorized/in-flight requests may still finish normally; the UI must not promise recall of those operations.

Basis: D-197, D-249, D-279, D-289. Alternate link/error state is described here but not separately pictured in this pilot.

N01 — Main menu

Layout: Play, Manage decks and Contacts are large icon-plus-text destinations. Android notification settings is a smaller text link to OS settings, not a new in-app preferences suite. Logout is separately labeled. “alex” is an example username, not the authenticated service account used to produce these designs.

Interaction: Play opens P01; Manage decks opens D01; Contacts opens P02. Logout immediately clears this device’s login and private downloads, returning to A01 without deleting server games/decks or logging out independent devices. Remote revocation is best effort. This proposed layout does not add a routine logout confirmation or expose account-email data in shared player lists.

Basis: D-188, D-196, D-218, D-220, D-241, D-282, D-289.

P01 — Games and invitations

Layout: explicitly separated invitation, active-game and lobby sections. Accept/Decline, Open, Open lobby, Reinvite and New game are text actions; status labels are not action buttons. Landscape gives lists separate columns.

Interaction: Accept enters the exact existing lobby as L02, without Ready or an immediate start. Decline retains the inviter’s lobby/preparation/Ready. Reinvite addresses that lobby, not a replacement game. Invitations do not expire automatically; cancelling a game removes its invitation and current listing. Open active game reaches G00 in this pilot. New game opens P02. An empty list would show “No current games” with New game, not a finished-game archive.

Basis: D-188, D-195, D-208, D-209, D-214, D-287. Empty/loading states are not separate mockups yet; no unread/read, presence or result statistics are implied.

P02 — Contacts and new game

Layout: Search usernames is a field; search magnifier is a supporting icon. Search, Add contact and Invite are labeled text actions. Saved contacts and search results remain separate. No email addresses or online-status dots.

Interaction: Search produces explicit username matches; Add contact saves a contact directly with no friend-request approval. A newly saved contact gets Invite in the contact list. Invite creates a game plus its first invitation and opens L01. There is no extra confirmation/selection wizard or automatic recipient acceptance. No results uses an inline “No matching usernames” notice, not a missing-user substitution. Removing contacts is not invented by this pilot.

Basis: D-195, D-196, D-197, D-218. Exact search matching is not settled by these example names or the placement of the Search button.

D01 — Saved decks

Layout: named deck rows/cards use cover placeholders and descriptive mainboard/sideboard counts. Import deck is a labeled text action with a supporting icon. Opening a deck goes to D02. An empty collection keeps Import deck visible.

Interaction: collection names/lists/covers synchronize between the account’s devices. Saved card-list changes happen through import, not individual quantity editors or a deck-builder search. No Export, legality badge, restore bin, win-rate statistics or gameplay Undo for collection deletion. Missing artwork uses the deck/card text fallback and does not prevent import or deck selection.

Basis: D-189, D-198, D-199, D-218, D-221, D-241, D-271.

D02 — Saved deck details

Layout: Name/Rename and cover/Choose cover are metadata controls. Re-import and Delete saved deck are text actions. Mainboard/Sideboard tabs only choose which read-only saved list is displayed; they are not in-game zone controls. Landscape puts metadata beside that list.

Interaction: proposed Rename opens a small name-field dialog with Save name and Cancel; it cannot change card quantities. Choose cover opens D05. Re-import opens D03 with this saved deck as a replacement candidate. Delete opens D06. Saving or deleting this collection entry never rewrites copies already selected in a lobby/game. Card names and counts in the mockup are illustrative synthetic data, not a real valid import or a required deck-size rule.

Basis: D-189, D-199, D-221. Rename’s edit state is described but not separately pictured; naming/duplicate policies are not inferred from the example.

D03 — Import with unresolved names

Layout: Deck list is a multiline text field, not a card builder. The error identifies the unresolved line. Review import is unavailable while entries are unresolved. Landscape uses an input/issues split; input and feedback must both remain reachable rather than squeezing the text area into a one-line field.

Interaction: accept ordinary quantity/name lists, common optional printing suffixes and supported mainboard/sideboard separators. Correct the pasted text or retry lookup; never silently choose an ambiguous card or save a partial list. Nothing replaces a saved deck on lookup/transport failure. When all entries resolve, Review import advances to D04. Art downloading and obtaining the newest entire catalog are not save prerequisites. No separate Send/definition-upload UI.

Basis: D-198, D-271, D-289. The misspelled synthetic entry deliberately models an error; these fake card names do not claim compatibility with a live catalog. D04 uses a separate complete sample, not the computed count of this short list.

D04 — Resolved import and save choice

Layout: resolved counts and a read-only preview accompany a Deck name field. Save as new / Replace saved deck is an explicit mode choice; replacement identifies the target collection entry. Save deck and Edit pasted list are text actions. Cover selection is optional later metadata, not a forced extra import step.

Interaction: Save as new creates a distinct saved entry; Replace changes the selected saved entry only. Neither changes a lobby/game’s selected copy. Save requires fully resolved definitions and atomic server acceptance; failure retains the previous valid saved deck and editable input. Success returns to D02 (or the calling lobby deck picker when import was launched there). This ordinary form save is not a gameplay Send gate or proof of format legality.

Basis: D-198, D-199, D-221, D-271, D-289. The two-step input/review presentation is proposed and can be simplified during owner review.

D04b — Import review: save controls

Same screen, different scroll position: expose the bottom of D04, including Save deck and Edit pasted list. Long content scrolls; no target shrinks to fit. The selected Save as new example still applies. Choosing Replace instead uses the existing-deck selector on this same form, not an additional Send/upload step. This extra view is a UI-review continuation, not another mandatory route screen.

D05 — Choose a deck cover

Layout: card-name tiles are selectable thumbnails, not card-edit controls. The selected tile has an outline/check plus text. Use selected card confirms the metadata choice; Cancel/Back leaves it unchanged. Landscape uses the short width efficiently while allowing the grid to scroll.

Interaction: select one card already in this deck as its cover. No image upload, crop tool, outside-catalog cover choice or mutation of that card. Text fallback remains available while art is absent. The small selection/confirmation step is a reviewable UI proposal, not a new game-action confirmation requirement. Cover fallback after a later re-import is not decided by these example tiles.

Basis: D-199, D-271.

D06 — Delete a saved deck

Layout: a bounded modal over the collection, with Keep deck and Delete saved deck as text buttons. The destructive button is distinguished by wording as well as styling. Background rows are not interactive while the modal is open.

Interaction: Keep deck/Back cancels this dialog without deleting anything. Delete saved deck requests collection deletion and returns to D01 after success. Selected game/lobby copies survive. No trash folder, gameplay Undo or misleading “Undo deletion” snackbar is offered. A failed deletion reports its actual failure without optimistically claiming permanent success. This one destructive-data confirmation is a proposal, not a universal confirm-every-action policy.

Basis: D-221, D-241; exact confirmation presentation is UI design work.

L01 — Lobby awaiting invitation acceptance

Layout: own deck/preparation, recipient invitation status, starter choice and Ready are distinct. Ready is enabled because this example has an own selected deck, even though riley has not accepted. Cancel game is separate from Back. Random is an illustrative selected value, not an approved universal default.

Interaction: Change deck opens L03; Prepare deck opens L04. Ready can persist before acceptance. The opponent’s later acceptance opens this same lobby without resetting the inviter’s preparation or Ready. Decline retains it and permits Reinvite through the existing-lobby path. Cancel game removes this pending invite and its game; merely leaving the screen does neither. No host Start or expiry.

Basis: D-195, D-201, D-204–D-209, D-287.

L02 — Accepted lobby before own deck selection

Layout: Choose deck is the own-side primary action. Opponent Ready is an explicit status with text/checkmark, not permission to start for them. Own Ready is disabled with the visible reason “Select your deck.” Starter offers either participant or Random; it is not a pre-start reroll.

Interaction: Accepting P01 did not select a deck, Ready or immediately start. Select an existing saved deck through L03; no legality or size check is added. After selection, Prepare deck and enabled Ready use L01/L05’s layout with accepted opponent status. Changes to own deck/preparation/starter clear only the changing player’s Ready. Late lobby edits after the game starts fail normally; the screen must move to the actual active game rather than reopening the lobby.

Basis: D-190, D-191, D-195, D-201, D-204, D-205, D-274.

L03 — Select a game-local deck copy

Layout: saved deck name, cover fallback and descriptive counts accompany each Select text action. Import deck is a secondary escape when the collection lacks the desired deck, not a required detour for normal selection.

Interaction: Select creates/replaces this game’s prepared copy and returns directly to its lobby. It clears own Ready without affecting the opponent’s. It does not edit the saved source, auto-ready or require another Send/confirmation. Deleting/editing the source later leaves this copy intact. Back cancels the picker without changing selection. An empty collection uses the same Import route; there is no automatic blank deck or silent substitute.

Basis: D-189, D-191, D-199, D-205, D-221.

L04 — Prepare mainboard and sideboard

Layout: Mainboard / Library and Sideboard are separate labeled list panels. Selected rows and explicit Move 1 text actions provide discoverable transfer controls without depending on drag precision. Landscape uses equal independently scrollable columns; portrait stacks them. Quantity/name rows summarize copies, not saved-deck editing privileges.

Interaction: choose a row and transfer one copy in either direction; repeat as desired, with no one-for-one or legal-size enforcement. Completed transfers automatically synchronize, clear only own Ready and leave the saved deck alone. No Save preparation/Done-to-send is required. Back simply returns to the lobby. On entering actual play, no Sideboard view/edit/move path exists. The shown per-copy list controls are proposals, not a finalized drag/drop or bulk design.

Basis: D-189, D-191, D-202, D-203, D-259.

L05 — Own Ready accepted

Layout: own Ready is a textual status/checkmark. Withdraw Ready is an explicit action; Change deck/Prepare deck remain discoverable. No host Start button or both-online indicator. Cancel game remains separate and applies only before start.

Interaction: Ready persists after leaving/disconnection; it is not a liveness lease. The second accepted Ready starts once, even while the first player is away. Start shuffles both Libraries, sets life to 20, resolves a selected Random starter and begins turn 1 at Untap, with no automatic opening draw. The pilot then shows G00. On returning after an accepted game ending, restore last prepared decks, clear both Ready and use this lobby structure in its not-ready state; both must ready again. Back alone never withdraws Ready or cancels the game.

Basis: D-190, D-200, D-204, D-205, D-213, D-274.

L06 — Cancel an unstarted game

Layout: proposed confirmation with Keep game / Cancel game text buttons. The dimmed background is a lobby, not a live game. Back/close keeps the game.

Interaction: either participant can request cancellation before start without the other player’s approval. It removes the current listing and pending invite; there is no trash/restore UI. Leaving the screen is different and preserves the lobby/Ready. If start already won the normal server ordering race, do not cancel or reset that started play; show the current game. Reinvitation must not revive a cancelled lobby. This dialog is not the gameplay result-suggestion/acceptance flow, which is intentionally excluded from the pilot.

Basis: D-205–D-209, D-241, D-287. The extra cancellation confirmation is a reviewable UI proposal, not approval of an extra gameplay-ending confirmation.

G00 — Gameplay intentionally omitted

Layout: only a shell, Back and a clearly labeled empty content area. This gives the non-gameplay navigation a destination and demonstrates two orientations. It does not settle how much space the real board, hand, history or controls get.

Interaction: active-game Open and lobby Start transitions terminate at this placeholder for the pilot. The real app’s start remains automatic on both Ready; there is no Start control here. Back returns to current games, not a shared game Undo, game cancellation or result suggestion. No Sideboard is shown during play.

Scope: live/historic/playback views, card menus, selection, dragging, combat, Stack, reveal, inspectors, history tree, chat and result coordination require a later gameplay design batch with the owner’s verbal guidance.

U01 — Reconnecting and downloaded read-only review

Layout: Reconnecting is a status dialog over the same deliberately empty area. Review downloaded data and Back to games are text navigation actions. This proposes a clear way out of the blocking dialog without enabling mutations.

Interaction: shared actions stay blocked while disconnected, including Undo, Ready, branch activation and new inspection requiring exposure logging. Downloaded read-only navigation remains available. This does not create offline actions or a manual-resend/recovery-center workflow. Same-process reconnect automatically recovers actual already-sent outcomes with original identities. Process restart instead syncs server state and may lose uncommitted local work. Unknown outcome is not rejection; the UI must not invite duplicate submission as a fresh action.

Basis: D-182, D-215, D-216, D-241, D-246, D-252, D-278. The exact dialog escape and wording are UI proposals; the gameplay contents remain undesigned.

Whole-journey interaction budgets

These are draft counts for the proposed route, not measured Android tests. A “tap” means one explicit activation; typing/pasting, scrolling and keyboard dismissal are additional interaction cost, not hidden zero-cost steps.

Starting state → goal Proposed route and explicit activations Additional work
Main menu → existing active game Play → Open: 2 taps. List scrolling if needed.
Main menu → accept a visible invite Play → Accept: 2 taps, arriving in the same lobby, not Ready. Scrolling if needed.
Main menu → invite a saved contact Contacts → Invite: 2 taps, arriving in waiting lobby. Contact-list scrolling if needed.
Main menu → search, add and invite Contacts → Search field → Search → Add contact → Invite: 5 taps. Type username; keyboard/scroll cost may add taps.
Main menu → save a new imported list Manage decks → Import → list field → Review import → name field → Save deck: 6 taps. Paste/type list and name; correction/keyboard/scroll cost.
Accepted lobby without a deck → Ready Choose deck → Select → Ready: 3 taps. Deck-list scrolling if needed. No legality/size confirmation.
Preparation open → transfer one copy Select row → Move 1: 2 taps. List scrolling if needed; repeated moves must not add a Send step.
Ready lobby → leave without withdrawing Back: 1 tap. No cancellation or publication prompt.
Saved-deck details → delete collection entry Delete saved deck → confirm deletion: 2 taps. Copies selected in games survive.

The import review split, cover confirmation and cancellation dialog are intentional pilot proposals whose interaction cost should be reviewed, not silently declared optimal. Reaching a visible button may require scrolling in short landscape or with a keyboard; the later large-text/keyboard review must count that cost too.

Coverage and limits

Pictured: 21 primary screen/state drafts and two scrolled continuations, all in both orientations: 46 captures. These include an inline sign-in error, submitted reset request, unresolved import, two import save modes in one state, collection-deletion modal, waiting invitation, no-own-deck lobby, preparation, accepted Ready, cancellation modal and reconnect dialog.

Described but not separately pictured: clean authentication forms, network and field errors, invalid reset link, empty/loading/search-no-results lists, rename editor, import lookup-in-progress/save failure, replacing-mode selection, returned-lobby not-ready state and successful reconnect. These still need visual state completion before claiming that every non-gameplay state is designed.

Not claimed: final visual style, full keyboard/large-text/tablet/foldable coverage, touch/accessibility usability validation, live Android behavior, exhaustive state/concurrency testing or a passed UI/review gate. Platform notification permission dialogs/settings belong to Android; this pilot includes their entry point, not fabricated custom mute/settings screens.

Behavior and UI discrepancies found during review are documentation/design work, not permission to add features or start application implementation.

Provenance and review artifacts

The layouts were requested from Google Stitch in the private design project 6617750535460836476 on 2026-10-21. Static HTML exports, generation briefs and the screen manifest are retained with this packet. Each responsive source is captured at both fixed viewports; no portrait screenshot is stretched to make a landscape image. Review captures, not Stitch’s default large canvas preview, are the images embedded here.

See generation briefs and source manifest. The exported HTML is design material with executable interactions removed, not production frontend/application scaffolding. Any documented normalization or repair of generated presentation is recorded in the manifest/build notes rather than silently attributed to Stitch.

Review repairs included removing Stitch-invented 60/15-card size restrictions from lobby/preparation wording, describing definition resolution rather than catalog authenticity, restoring a clipped landscape Back target and widening a landscape reset form that had accidentally retained its portrait width limit. The minimum-target normalization also makes some short landscape panels scroll; it must not be mistaken for a completed native accessibility review.

The UI draft index explains rebuild and private hosting. HTML and PDF are compiled from this same Markdown and use the same embedded image files. Review progress is not a separate source of game behavior.
